newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan will intervene when it can 'win'--Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Japan will intervene when it can 'win'--Sakakibara.

text.p: Japan will intervene in foreign exchange markets when it can "win", senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said on Wednesday.

Japanese authorities will intervene in foreign exchange markets when appropriate and when they see that it can be effective, Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's international finance bureau, said in a speech to currency dealers.
He added that he shared U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's view that authorities should intervene when appropriate, saying, "we will intervene when we think we can win."
Sakakibara said recent movements of the yen were clearly excessive and that Japan would take decisive action at an appropriate time.
He added that U.S. authorities shared this view.
"The U.S. Treasury shares this concern," Sakakibara said.
Market participants' view of the Japanese economy is overly pessimistic, he said, adding, "the Japanese economy is very healthy."
Sakakibara said the worst of Japanese banks' bad loan issue was now over.
He also said he could not comprehend why Japan's long-term interest rates were at their current record-low levels.
Sakakibara said that although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan, there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate.
"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," he said.
